name: Matrixyl 3000

lead: Matrixyl 3000 is a branded pairing of two lab-made peptides used in anti-wrinkle serums.
Independent published human data on the blend are limited.

paras: Its peptides are proposed to signal skin cells to repair matrix and reduce inflammation; one study found they stay in the skin surface layers.
A cosmetic ingredient; no blend-specific safety data were found in the sources reviewed.

web.title: Permeation behaviour of cosmetic actives into the human stratum corneum

lead: Matrixyl 3000 is a branded peptide complex made by Sederma that combines palmitoyl tripeptide-1 and palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7, and is used in anti-wrinkle serums. [1] Its predecessor, Matrixyl (palmitoyl pentapeptide-4), was launched by Sederma in 2000. [2]

Published evidence on the blend itself is limited: a 2026 permeation study reported that both peptides were detected in layers of the stratum corneum of three volunteers but appeared to remain between cells. [1]

paras: The two peptides are lipid-modified fragments proposed to signal skin cells about matrix repair and inflammation. A patent application lists oligopeptide derivatives with acyl groups combined with apple extract for wrinkles, tested in 42 women aged 40 to 70 around the eyes over four weeks. [3]

No independent trial of Matrixyl 3000 itself was found. The permeation study above examined its two peptides in serums on three volunteers. [1] Wikipedia states that efficacy statements on the original Matrixyl are tagged as needing medical citation. [2]
